> 故知般若波罗蜜多，是大神咒，是大明咒，是无上咒，是无等等咒，能除一切苦，真实不虚。
>
> 故说般若波罗蜜多咒，即说咒曰：揭谛揭谛，波罗揭谛，波罗僧揭谛，菩提萨婆诃。

After ten lines of dismantling, the sutra changes register. No more analysis, no more negations of lists. It turns the whole thing into a mantra and ends.

That switch is not decoration. 陀罗尼 does not mean spell in the sense of an incantation used to ward off harm; it means 总持 — total holding. One phrase holding the entire body of meaning. The preceding lines were 拆解, taking the apparatus apart piece by piece; the mantra is 收摄, gathering it back into a single act.

The pedagogy is the point: analysis multiplies, and a mind can analyze forever without arriving. The mantra refuses the multiplication. One turn of attention and the whole of it is present, not sequentially but at once.

## The five epithets

大神咒 — great, mysterious. 神 here is not the supernatural. It is what cannot be reached by calculation: the way seeing-through works without a plan, dissolving a grip nobody decided to release. Every deliberate maneuver in the mind is a scheme, and a scheme has a schemer; this operates outside that.

大明咒 — great, illuminating. 明 breaks 无明, which is not ignorance in the sense of missing information but the dark of taking a construction for a given. Light here does not add facts. It removes the confusion about what was already in front of you.

无上咒 — unsurpassed. Nothing above it, because everything above would have to be a level, and levels are inside the apparatus that has just been emptied.

无等等咒 — equal to nothing. Every paired dharma has a counterpart: high has low, pure has impure. This has no counterpart, which is a stronger claim than "supreme". Supreme still sits on a scale.

能除一切苦 — removes all suffering. Note the mechanism claimed: not that suffering stops occurring, but that its root is pulled. The root is the grip, and the grip is what the mantra addresses. A pain with no owner is a sensation; the same pain filed under a self is a life.

## The mantra itself

揭谛揭谛 — gate gate — go, go. Repeated. Not to fill a meter: the double is urging, the way a hand is waved toward a door.

波罗揭谛 — pāragate — gone to the far shore. 波罗 is the far shore, and the book is firm that this is not geography: not a location after death, not a realm entered in absorption. 迷的时候，处处是此岸 — deluded, every place is this shore; released, this shore is the other one.

波罗僧揭谛 — pārasaṃgate — gone together to the far shore. 僧 here is not the monastic order; it is 共, together. The line turns private liberation outward: not my crossing but the crossing, shared.

菩提萨婆诃 — bodhi svāhā — awakening, so be it. Svāhā is the closing that seals a statement: accomplished, may it be so. It is the one word in the sutra that sounds like a wish, and it is placed at the very end, after everything has been taken apart.

## What the mantra is not

Not a password. Not a transaction. The book is explicit that reciting the sounds cannot by itself cancel anything or purchase anything — that would be the acquisition model returning through the back door, wearing a robe.

It is a handle. Sound gathers attention when attention is scattered; the phrase holds the whole of the sutra in a form short enough to be held. What is held is not the words. What is held is the direction.

渡而无渡，无渡而渡 — crossing with no crossing, no crossing and crossing.

## The test

Say the mantra once, slowly, and notice what your attention does at 揭谛揭谛. Does it speed up, anticipating the end? Does it go flat, reciting on rails?

Then say it once more without trying to fix either. The difference between the two recitations is the whole distance the sutra has been describing.
